A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RLAAR study. Their text, equations, tables, figure, examples, and pseudocode support reliable comparison, including matching the retained appendices across renumbering and repagination.

before.justification: Tables 1–3 report original RLAAR evaluations and ablations on Qwen models, alongside explicitly borrowed results for other models.

after.justification: v2 retains the original RLAAR experiments and adds supervised fine-tuning comparisons in Table 1 and human–LLM agreement results in Appendix A, Table 4.

M1.justification: The three rollout types, accuracy and abstention rewards, and three-stage curriculum remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 are retained, with the pseudocode appendix renumbered from B to C.

E1.justification: Training retains GSM8K and the Eurus code subset; evaluation retains math, code, database, and actions. The new human validation samples existing solvable and unsolvable math scenarios without expanding task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds a supervised fine-tuning comparison using Gemini-2.5-Pro distillation for Qwen3-8B and Qwen2.5-7B. This introduces one additional comparison approach while retaining the existing comparator set.

E3.justification: Appendix A introduces human validation on 100 randomly sampled math examples, split into 50 solvable and 50 unsolvable cases, comparing human abstention labels with GPT-4o judgments. Existing RLAAR training settings and benchmark evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new Appendix A/Table 4 tests whether the automated abstention evaluator agrees with human judgments. The abstention-ratio and curriculum ablations in Tables 2–3, and the failure/success examples, are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for its experiments. Table 4 adds agreement point estimates without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Existing scores in Tables 1–3 are unchanged. New SFT rows report average LiC/Abstain scores of 62.7/49.0 for Qwen3-8B and 55.0/50.1 for Qwen2.5-7B. Table 4 adds human–LLM agreement of 0.92 for the Qwen2.5-7B baseline and 0.97 for RLAAR.

T1.justification: Section 3 retains the same finite-horizon MDP formulation, binary reward definitions in Equations 1–3, and curriculum threshold mathematics. No theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about multi-turn RL, mixed rewards, curriculum learning, and mitigating LiC. The headline results are unchanged; the revised title does not redefine the contribution.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 adds the interpretation that the tested distillation baselines offer little LiC mitigation. Appendix A explicitly characterizes GPT-4o as an abstention-intent classifier and interprets human agreement as supporting metric reliability. The existing applicability limitation remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 identifies Gemini-2.5-Pro as the SFT distillation teacher and documents the human-validation sample size, solvability balance, and labeling target. Existing RLAAR hyperparameters, hardware, and Verl reference remain unchanged; detailed SFT training and annotation instructions are not supplied.

R1.justification: The related-work sections and bibliography are unchanged. Gemini-2.5-Pro was already cited and evaluated in v1, and the paper retains its positioning around multi-turn RL, abstention, and curriculum learning.

P1.justification: v2 revises the title, expands the author and affiliation block, makes small prose edits, and adds an evaluation-metrics appendix. Examples and pseudocode shift from Appendices A/B to B/C, with updated references; the main narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains two SFT rows and explicit RLAAR labels, and Table 4 is added. Appendix introductory text changes to two columns, examples are repaginated, and page-number footers are removed. Figure 1 and the existing ablation displays are retained.

improvement.justification: The added SFT comparisons address a missing training alternative, while Appendix A supplies a focused human check for the previously unvalidated GPT-4o abstention evaluator. These additions modestly strengthen the evidence. Their value is limited by the validation's 100-example math-only scope and the sparse documentation of SFT training and human annotation.
